task_description: Add a configurable Start menu to the Ubuntu White Edition GNOME desktop: a Start button fixed at the bottom-left of the White Edition panel whose Start-menu popup opens left, center, or right per a user Setting (default left), plus an Ubuntu-themed selectable Start-button logo with 3 candidate SVGs. Implemented as an additive White Edition GNOME Shell extension with a GSettings schema and prefs UI, per the shell-extension layer the White Edition README already calls for. Documented, committed on branch feat/white-edition-start-menu.

verification.summary: No compile/test harness for this additive JS + XML + SVG + docs layer; verification is the project's static suite and it passes. node --check clean on extension.js and prefs.js; glib-compile-schemas --strict clean on the gschema; xmllint --noout clean on all 3 logo SVGs and the gschema; bash -n clean on install.sh. Wiring grep-confirmed: metadata uuid == dirname white-edition@mearvk, settings-schema == gschema id org.gnome.shell.extensions.white-edition, shell-version [46,47]; Start button added unconditionally to panel 'left' box at position 0 (fixed bottom-left) while only the popup boxpointer x depends on start-menu-alignment (enum left|center|right, default left); start-button-logo enum (circle-of-friends|mono-accent|focus-ring, default circle-of-friends) read in both extension.js and prefs.js. No em dashes, no vendored upstream GNOME source modified, no compiled artifacts committed. test_quality: there is no test suite; the static validators are meaningful (they parse/compile the actual authored files and would fail on real errors). Docker skipped: no Dockerfile for this layer and network restricted. Runtime behavior (live popup anchoring, GSettings binding, Adw/Gtk4 prefs rendering) not verifiable without a live GNOME Shell and is documented as a caveat in the extension README.
